ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, rectangle $OABC$ is in a Cartesian coordinate system, with the coordinate of vertex $B$ being $\left(4, n\right)$. Diagonals $OB$ and $AC$ intersect at $D$. The line $y=\frac{3}{4}nx-\frac{3}{2}n$ intersects $OA$, $AC$, and $OB$ at $P$, $M$, and $N$, respectively. Find the length of $DP$ (expressed in terms of $n$).
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral OABC is a rectangle,\\
it follows that point D is the midpoint of OB,\\
Since $O(0,0)$ and $B(4,n)$,\\
it follows that $D(2,\frac{n}{2})$,\\
From $\frac{3}{4}nx-\frac{3}{2}n=0$ we get: $x=2$, therefore $P(2,0)$,\\
thus $DP\parallel$ y-axis,\\
thus $DP=\boxed{\frac{n}{2}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, OA goes to the right along the x-axis, OC goes upward along the y-axis, and OABC forms a rectangle; B is located at the upper right corner. The two diagonals OB and AC of the rectangle are drawn in the figure, and they intersect at D. There is also an oblique straight line that intersects OA at P, intersects AC at M, and intersects OB at N. In the figure, P is on the x-axis, and D is located near directly above P. Reasoning: It is known that O=(0,0), B=(4,n). The diagonals of a rectangle bisect each other, so D is the midpoint of diagonal OB, therefore D=((0+4)/2,(0+n)/2)=(2,n/2). Point P is on OA, and OA is the x-axis, so the y-coordinate of P is 0. Substitute y=0 into the straight-line equation y=(3/4)nx-(3/2)n, obtaining 0=(3/4)nx-(3/2)n. Since the height of the rectangle in the figure is n, and B is above the x-axis, take n>0, so it can be divided by n, obtaining (3/4)x=3/2, namely x=2. Therefore P=(2,0). The x-coordinates of D and P are the same, DP is a vertical line segment, and its length is |n/2-0|=n/2.
